choices.text: Store the raw responses in a spreadsheet maintained by the compliance team
Keep prompt version, model id and input reference per row; keep raw responses for a retention window plus sampled rows; document it
Store nothing beyond the extracted values themselves, since the storage cost of 50 million responses outweighs the compliance team's need
Store everything forever, regardless of cost, since compliance always takes priority

stem: An LLM extraction over supplier PDFs works well for English documents but produces empty or wrong fields for the 15% of documents in Japanese. What should be done?

choices.text: Exclude the Japanese documents from the pipeline and handle them manually, since the model evidently does not support that language well enough
Ask the supplier to send documents in English only
Translate every incoming document to English with a second model call before the extraction step, regardless of the additional cost and latency
Check the extracted text (OCR, encoding), the prompt's language assumptions and the model's multilingual capability; fix that stage and add Japanese cases

stem: A team wants to evaluate an agent that must choose the right tool among four for each request. Which metric design measures this?

choices.text: Overall answer accuracy only, since a correct final answer implies that the right tool must have been chosen somewhere along the way
Tool-selection accuracy per test case, comparing the tools called with the expected calls, alongside answer accuracy
Latency per request, since choosing the wrong tool usually makes the request slower
The total number of tool calls per session, where fewer calls always indicates better tool selection

stem: An evaluation suite for a grounded assistant has 300 answerable questions. A reviewer asks for cases that test what the assistant does when the corpus has no answer. How should these be constructed?

choices.text: Write questions whose answers are genuinely absent from the corpus, expecting an explicit "not found", scored for refusal and no invented content
Ask questions in a foreign language, since the assistant will not be able to answer them
Reuse the existing answerable questions but delete their expected answers from the suite, so that any response the assistant gives counts as a failure
Ask extremely vague questions, since vagueness guarantees an unanswerable case

stem: A team runs its evaluation suite nightly. Scores fluctuate between 86% and 92% with no changes to the function. A manager wants to set a pass threshold at 90%. What should the engineer advise?

choices.text: Stop running the suite nightly, since fluctuating scores are not informative
Set the threshold at 90% as requested and treat any nightly run that scores below it as a regression requiring an immediate rollback of the function
Measure run-to-run variance first, set the threshold relative to that distribution, and reduce variance (temperature, suite size) where possible
Set the threshold at 86% so the suite never fails

stem: Which evaluator is appropriate for checking that a function's extracted invoice total matches the expected value?

choices.text: A string similarity score between the extracted and expected totals formatted as text, passing when the similarity is above 90%
Human review of every case, since numbers are too important to automate
A model-graded rubric asking whether the total "seems reasonable" given the invoice
A deterministic numeric comparison with exact match, or a tolerance only where rounding is legitimate

stem: An automated workflow approves or rejects document submissions. Downstream, human reviewers sometimes overturn its decisions. How should these overturns be used?

choices.text: Ignore them, since reviewers and the workflow apply different standards and the workflow's metrics are already tracked
Reduce the workflow's authority so that every submission goes to human review from now on, since the overturns prove the workflow cannot be trusted
Retrain the model on overturned cases every week so that the workflow aligns with the reviewers automatically
Capture each overturn with input and both decisions, turn confirmed cases into evaluation cases, analyze by failure type, and prioritize fixes

stem: An agent can execute an Action that changes a customer's contract terms. Which evaluation cases are essential before release?

choices.text: Authorized requests (execute), unauthorized users (no change), ambiguous evidence (escalate) and injected instructions (ignore), checked on the objects
Cases where the request is clear and the user is authorized, to confirm that the Action works end to end and the contract object is updated
Cases that check the politeness of the agent's responses to customers
Cases that measure how quickly the Action executes under load

stem: After switching the grading model used by an evaluation suite, every function's score rose by about 5 points overnight with no changes to the functions. What happened and what should be done?

choices.text: The functions improved because the new grader gives the model better feedback during evaluation; the higher scores should be reported as progress
Nothing happened; a 5-point rise across all functions is normal variance
The grader changed, so scores are no longer comparable; calibrate the new grader against human ratings and re-baseline all functions
The old grader was broken; the new scores are the true ones and history should be deleted

stem: A team wants to compare three prompt variants for a summarization function fairly. Which experiment design is correct?

choices.text: Run the variants in production on alternate days and compare user complaints
Run all three on the same fixed suite with the same model, settings and evaluators, repeated to estimate variance, and compare per case
Run each variant on different random samples of documents and compare average scores
Let each engineer test their own variant on documents they choose themselves and present the best examples to the team for a vote

stem: An AI workflow should process orders in batches overnight when a daily feed lands, not one by one as they arrive. Which Automate configuration matches this?

choices.text: A property-change trigger on each order's status, which runs the workflow whenever any status changes during the day
A schedule-based or input-update trigger that runs once when the daily feed has landed and processes the day's orders as a set
An object-created trigger that fires per order, since every order must eventually be processed and per-object execution is the default
A manual trigger that an operator presses each morning after checking that the feed arrived

stem: An AI function returns a recommended discount for a quote. The business requires that any discount above 15% is applied only after a manager approves. How should the function's output reach the quote object?

choices.text: The function returns a recommendation; an Action applies it, and discounts above 15% create an approval task applied only on approval
The function applies the discount directly through an Ontology edit, and a separate report lists discounts above 15% for managers to review afterwards
The function is told in its prompt never to recommend more than 15%, which removes the need for approval
The function writes the discount to a notes field, and sales staff copy it to the quote manually

stem: An automation that sends AI-generated notifications ran twice for the same event after a platform restart, and recipients received duplicate messages. What design change prevents a repeat?

choices.text: Add a delay of ten minutes before every send so that duplicates are spaced out
Disable the automation during every planned platform maintenance window and re-enable it afterwards by hand once the restart is confirmed
Make the send idempotent with a per-event delivery marker, skipping sends when the marker exists
Reduce the number of recipients so duplicates affect fewer people

stem: A multi-step workflow extracts data with an AI function, validates it, writes an object via an Action, and then calls an external system. The external call sometimes fails after the object is written. What should the design ensure?

choices.text: That the whole workflow is re-run from the beginning on any failure, including the AI extraction
That the external call happens before the object is written, so a failed call leaves nothing behind
That failures are ignored for now, since the object is already written and the external system can be reconciled against it by a monthly report
That the object records the external call's status, retries resume from that step only, and the call carries an idempotency key

stem: An automation should run an AI function for every new ticket but must not run while a related nightly data migration is in progress, which would give the function inconsistent data. What is the appropriate control?

choices.text: Delete tickets that arrive during the migration and ask users to resubmit
Add a condition that checks the migration status before processing and defers tickets until the migration completes
Tell the AI function in its prompt to be careful during migrations
Schedule the automation to run only during business hours, on the assumption that data migrations always happen overnight and finish before morning

stem: A team must change a live automation so that it also writes a second property. The change is approved. Which rollout minimizes risk?

choices.text: Deploy the change and immediately reprocess all historical objects in one run so that every object has the new property populated from the start
Pause the automation for a week while the change is developed, then resume with the new behaviour
Edit the live automation directly, since adding a property cannot break anything
Make the change in a new version or branch, test on representative objects, deploy at low traffic with monitoring and rollback ready

stem: A Workshop user needs to trigger an AI analysis of a selected object and see the result immediately, while an operations process needs the same analysis run automatically for every new object. Which integration serves both without duplicating logic?

choices.text: The automation path only, with Workshop users waiting for the nightly run to see results
The Workshop path only, with operations staff clicking the button for every new object
One published function, called by a function-backed Action from Workshop and as an effect by the Automate rule, sharing one version
Two separate implementations of the analysis, one for the Workshop button and one for the automation, so each can be tuned and released independently

stem: An automation applies AI-recommended price updates through an Action. One night the AI function began returning prices ten times too high due to a unit confusion, and 300 products were updated before anyone noticed. Which safeguards should have been in place?

choices.text: Action validation (price band, maximum change), volume limits on the automation, and an anomaly alert, so the bad batch is blocked and surfaced
Manual approval of every single price change by a pricing manager before it is applied, regardless of the size of the change or the product
A nightly email listing all price changes for review the next morning
A larger model, which would not have confused the units

stem: A legal summarization workflow handles 200 long contracts per day; quality matters more than speed, and the budget allows a premium model. A reference sheet shows a top-tier model with a large context window and higher cost, and a mid-tier model with a smaller window. Which selection is justified?

choices.text: Whichever model the team used last time, to keep configurations consistent across workflows
The top-tier model with the larger context window, verified on the suite, because the task is high-value, low-volume and long-document
The top-tier model for the first 100 contracts and the mid-tier for the rest, to average the cost
The mid-tier model, since the cheaper option is always the right default for any workflow regardless of the task's quality or length requirements

stem: A workflow's execution history shows a growing number of runs ending in "timeout" over the last two weeks, with no change to the workflow. Which investigation sequence is right?

choices.text: Restart the workflow and its dependencies, since timeouts that appear after a long period of normal operation usually indicate a stuck process somewhere
Increase the timeout immediately and move on, since timeouts simply mean the limit is too low
Switch to a faster model, since model latency is the only stage that can cause a timeout
Use traces of timed-out runs to find which stage grew, correlate it with inputs or dependencies, fix that stage, and set a timeout with a fallback

stem: An agent answers the same 50 frequently asked policy questions thousands of times a day, alongside a long tail of unique questions. Costs are high. Which optimization is appropriate?

choices.text: Cache answers for recurring context-independent questions, keyed on normalized question and policy version; unique questions still run fully
Cache every answer the agent ever gives and serve the cached one whenever the new question is somewhat similar
Lower the model's temperature so that repeated questions generate identical answers, which the provider bills at a discounted rate for repeated output
Refuse to answer the frequently asked questions and point users to the policy document

stem: A company registers a custom model endpoint and a provider-hosted catalog model for the same workflow. Which is the right role for each, and what must be verified?

choices.text: Use the custom endpoint only, since self-hosted models are always more secure
Alternate between them randomly to balance the load
Define primary and fallback by evaluation and policy; verify both pass the suite, meet residency rules, and are visible in observability
Use the catalog model only, since custom endpoints are meant for experimentation and are not supported for production workflows

stem: A trace shows a workflow calling the model four times in sequence: classify, extract, validate with the model, and summarize. Each call is short, but the end-to-end latency is dominated by the four round-trips. What should the engineer consider?

choices.text: Accepting the latency, since multi-step workflows are inherently slow
Adding a fifth call that decides whether the other four are needed
Merging all four steps into one large prompt regardless of the effect on accuracy, since fewer model calls is always better for latency and cost
Run independent steps in parallel, replace model-based validation with deterministic checks, and merge steps only where the suite shows no loss

stem: A product owner asks for proof that a new AI feature is "working well" after two weeks in production. Which evidence from observability answers this properly?

choices.text: Volume, success and failure rates, latency distribution, cost trends, tool-call patterns, user feedback, and the suite score versus baseline
The provider's monthly invoice showing increased usage
A screenshot of one impressive conversation
The number of distinct users who opened the feature during the two weeks, since adoption by users is the clearest sign of success

stem: Which situation most justifies routing a request to a more capable (and more expensive) model within a workflow that otherwise uses a mid-tier model?

choices.text: Requests that arrive during business hours, when users are more demanding and more likely to notice a lower-quality answer
Every request, to be safe
Requests the mid-tier model flags as low-confidence or fails validation on, plus pre-identified high-consequence request types
Requests from the engineering team, who can judge the quality difference

stem: Cost for an AI workflow doubled last month. Token telemetry shows input tokens per request are unchanged, but requests per day doubled. What should the engineer conclude and do?

choices.text: The prompt has become too long; shorten it to cut the cost back
The increase is volume-driven; investigate where the extra requests come from (new consumer, retries, a loop, growth) before changing the workflow
Reduce the maximum output tokens, which halves cost regardless of volume
Switch to a cheaper model immediately, since the doubled bill shows that cost is the metric that matters most to the business right now

stem: A new team wants to use a particular catalog model in their workflows but the model is not enabled for their enrollment. Who resolves this and how?

choices.text: Enrollment administrators enable the model for that enrollment after reviewing policy, cost and data handling; the team requests it
The AI engineer edits the workflow to call the provider's API directly with a personal API key, bypassing the enrollment configuration until it is enabled
The team trains their own copy of the model so that no enablement is needed
The team copies another team's workflow that already uses the model, which carries the permission with it

stem: A workflow generates recommendations that are written to Ontology objects. Later, an auditor asks which recommendations were produced by which prompt and model version during March. How should the workflow have recorded this?

choices.text: Nowhere, since the Ontology stores values rather than how they were produced
In the engineer's personal notes about which prompts were in use when
As properties on each recommendation object: prompt version, model id, workflow version, timestamp and a trace reference
In the commit history of the prompt repository, from which the auditor can reconstruct which prompt was live on each day of March

stem: An AI workflow screens job applications and ranks candidates for recruiters. What governance design is appropriate for this high-consequence use?

choices.text: Automated ranking with the top ten advanced automatically and the rest rejected by email
The workflow produces explainable summaries and flags, recruiters make every decision, outputs are evaluated for bias, and its limits are documented
Fully automated rejection of the bottom half of the ranking, since the model applies the same criteria consistently and saves recruiters considerable time
No AI at all, since any use of AI in hiring is inappropriate

stem: A customer-facing agent was manipulated by a user into adopting a persona that ignored its guidelines and produced inappropriate content. Which combination of controls addresses this?

choices.text: Only a longer system prompt repeating the guidelines more firmly
Banning the user who did it and taking no other action, since the agent behaves perfectly well with normal users who do not try to manipulate it
Replacing the agent with a static FAQ page
Layered controls: hardened instructions, input/output safety checks, narrow scope and tools, monitoring, and jailbreak cases in the suite

stem: A function must run with elevated permissions to update records across many customers, but it is triggered by individual users from an app. What execution security design is appropriate?

choices.text: Disable permission checks for the function, since it is trusted code
Run it under a least-privilege service identity, restrict who may invoke it, validate inputs, and audit each run with the triggering user
Run the function as the triggering user and ask the administrators to make every app user an administrator so that the updates always succeed
Grant every app user the elevated permissions so the function works for all of them

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate way to handle a dataset of customer conversations, containing personal data, that a team wants to use to build a retrieval corpus for an internal agent?

choices.text: Index the conversations in a separate environment with no access controls, since retrieval only returns short chunks and never exposes the raw data
Remove only customer names and index everything else, since names are the only personal data
Minimize and redact personal data not needed, keep markings and access controls on the chunks, restrict the agent's audience, and document the purpose
Index the conversations as they are, since the agent is internal and employees are trusted

stem: A workflow drafts financial communications to clients. Regulators require that a qualified person reviews each communication before it is sent, and that the review is evidenced. How should the workflow be built?

choices.text: Have the model review its own draft and record that the review took place
Send the drafts automatically and keep copies of every communication so that qualified reviewers can look at them later if a regulator asks
Ask the client to confirm the communication looks correct after receiving it
Generate the draft, create a review task for a qualified reviewer, record their decision on the object, and send via an approval-gated Action

stem: An agent uses a web-browsing tool to gather public information. Security notes that fetched pages could contain instructions that manipulate the agent. What control set is appropriate for this tool?

choices.text: Treat fetched content as data: isolate it in the context, forbid Actions based on it alone, allow-list domains, scan for injection, test adversarially
Ask the agent in its instructions to ignore any instructions it finds on web pages, and consider the risk handled once that line is in the prompt
Trust pages from large well-known sites, since they do not contain injections
Remove the browsing tool, since any fetched content is untrusted

stem: A Logic function must produce a customer-facing message in the customer's preferred language, which is stored as a property on the Customer object passed as input. How should the prompt be built?

choices.text: Always write in English and translate afterwards with a second function
Ask the model to guess the customer's language from their name and write accordingly
Inject the language property into the task prompt as a variable, instruct the model to write in it, and return the language in the typed output
Write one prompt per supported language as separate Logic functions and ask every caller to pick the right function for each customer it processes

stem: Which of the following is the best reason to use a tool-using reasoning block instead of a single completion in AIP Logic?

choices.text: The task requires the model to decide from the input which lookups or functions to call and to use their results
The task requires a lower temperature than usual, and temperature can only be configured on tool-using reasoning blocks
The task's output must be a structured object with several typed fields rather than a plain string of text
The task needs a long and detailed answer that would not fit comfortably in the output of a single completion block

stem: A Logic function with an Ontology edit block works in testing but, in production, some edits are rejected with validation errors from the Action it uses. What is the right response?

choices.text: Retry the rejected edits until they pass
Bypass the Action and write directly to the dataset
Remove the Action's validation rules so that the function's edits always succeed in production the way they did during testing
Treat the rejections as the Action doing its job: inspect them, fix the function's output to satisfy the constraints, and add the cases to the suite

stem: An engineer wants to test a Logic function change against the same inputs that caused a production incident last week. What should they use?

choices.text: New synthetic inputs invented to resemble the incident
The stored inputs from the incident runs' traces, replayed against the draft as evaluation cases, so the test uses exactly what failed
The current production objects that were involved in the incident, even though some of them may have been edited since the incident happened
The function's system prompt, read carefully

stem: A Logic function sometimes receives inputs with missing optional fields (no phone number, no account manager). How should the prompt and blocks handle this?

choices.text: Fail the function whenever any field is missing
Make the fields optional in the typed input, handle absence with conditionals or explicit "not provided" injection, and test with and without them
Fill missing fields with made-up default values inside the function so that the prompt template is always complete and the model never sees a gap
Ignore the issue since models handle missing text fine

stem: Users report that a Logic function has become slower over the past month. Traces show the function's prompt now includes the full text of every linked document because a loop was added to inject them all. What should the engineer change?

choices.text: Remove the loop entirely and stop injecting any linked documents into the prompt, so the function answers from the object's own properties only
Ask users to link fewer documents
Increase the model's context window
Bound the context: inject only relevant documents or sections (metadata or semantic search), cap count and size, and verify with the suite

stem: A team wants a Logic function to summarize a meeting and then create follow-up Task objects for each action item. Which structure is safest?

choices.text: A completion producing a typed list of action items, a validation block (owners exist, dates valid), then an edit per validated item with invalid ones reported
Create Tasks first and summarize afterwards
Ask the model to create as many Tasks as it thinks are appropriate
One completion that writes the summary and creates all the Tasks in a single Ontology edit block without any validation checks in between

stem: Two versions of a Logic function differ only in temperature (0.2 versus 0.8). The evaluation suite scores them equally on accuracy, but the 0.8 version has twice the variance across runs. The function feeds an automation. Which version should be published?

choices.text: Alternate between the two versions on successive runs so that the automation gets the average of their behaviour over time
The 0.8 version, since variety in a model's outputs is generally desirable and prevents the automation from becoming too predictable
The 0.2 version, since an automation benefits from consistent outputs and lower variance makes regressions easier to detect
Neither, until the variance of both is zero

stem: An agent helps analysts explore a large Ontology. Its retrieval context currently includes every object type's documentation, making each turn slow and the answers unfocused. What should be changed about its context?

choices.text: Ask the analysts to type the relevant object type names at the start of every message
Remove all documentation from the context and let the model infer the Ontology's structure from object and property names as it goes
Keep all of the documentation in the standing context, since the agent might need any part of it on any turn and omitting something risks wrong answers
Replace the static dump with retrieval of only the object types and documentation relevant to the question, plus a short overview

stem: A company has an agent in AIP Agent Studio and wants Workshop users to interact with it inside a specific module, with the agent aware of the object the user has selected on screen. How is this achieved?

choices.text: By running the agent as a standalone page in another browser tab beside the Workshop module, where users can describe what they are looking at
By giving the agent a tool that lists all objects and asking it to guess which one the user means
By embedding the agent in the module and passing the selected object as application state, so its tools and prompts use the selection
By telling users to copy the selected object's id from the module and paste it into the chat at the start of every conversation with the agent

stem: An agent's guardrail is meant to stop it from giving legal advice. Testers find that asking "what would a lawyer say about this contract clause" bypasses it. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Define the boundary in instructions, add an output check for advice-like legal content, and add paraphrased adversarial cases to the suite
Add that exact phrase and a few obvious variants to a blocklist that rejects the message before the agent sees it
Remove the guardrail since it cannot be perfect
Lower the temperature so the agent is less creative and therefore less likely to drift into giving advice when asked indirect questions

stem: An agent will be used by external customers, not employees. What additional pre-release considerations apply compared with an internal agent?

choices.text: None; the same pre-release test plan applies to any agent regardless of who its users are, since the agent's logic is the same
Stricter adversarial testing, data scoped to the authenticated customer, rate and cost controls, refusal and escalation paths, and compliance review
Removing all tools so the agent can only chat
Only additional load testing, since the main difference with external users is that the traffic volume will be far higher than internal use

stem: A support agent should hand a conversation to a human when it cannot help. Which design makes this work well?

choices.text: Continuing to try different answers in a loop until the user either gets what they need or gives up and leaves the conversation
Ending the conversation with a generic "please call us" message and the support phone number whenever the agent cannot answer
A defined escalation path: recognized triggers, a summary of the conversation, a ticket or queue handoff with that summary, and clear next steps
Escalating every conversation to a human agent after the first exchange, so that no customer is ever left with an unresolved question

stem: Which statement about AIP Assist and a custom standard agent is accurate?

choices.text: Standard agents cannot be embedded in Workshop; only AIP Assist can
AIP Assist is the built-in helper for using the platform; standard agents are custom-built in Agent Studio with their own instructions, context and tools
AIP Assist replaces the need for any custom agents
AIP Assist can be configured with a company's custom tools and Ontology Actions just like a standard agent, so a separate agent is rarely needed

stem: An agent passes all evaluation cases but, in production, users often rephrase questions two or three times before getting a useful answer. What does this indicate and what should be done?

choices.text: The model should be replaced with a larger one, since a stronger model would understand the users' first phrasing without rephrasing
The agent should refuse rephrased questions and ask users to submit each question only once, which keeps conversations short
Users are asking poorly and need training on how to phrase questions, since the agent passes every case in the evaluation suite
The suite lacks real phrasings; sample production conversations, add messy and partial questions to the suite, and improve clarification behaviour

stem: Two agents are being designed. Agent A answers questions from a knowledge base. Agent B can submit refund requests up to a limit. How should their tool and permission configurations differ?

choices.text: Agent A gets read-only retrieval and no Actions; Agent B gets the refund Action with validation, limits, idempotency, audit and restricted invocation
Agent B should have fewer safeguards than Agent A since it is more useful to customers and safeguards would slow down legitimate refunds
Both should have the same tools and permissions for consistency, so that users get the same capabilities whichever agent they happen to use
Agent A should also have the refund Action in case users ask about refunds while reading the knowledge base, to avoid sending them elsewhere

stem: A team debates chunk overlap for a manual corpus. One engineer wants zero overlap to save storage; another wants 50% overlap "to be safe". What is the sound position?

choices.text: A modest overlap helps when answers span a boundary, while large overlaps add near-duplicates; pick the value by measuring retrieval quality
Zero overlap is always correct because duplicated text confuses the retriever and doubles the cost of every search over the index
Overlap is irrelevant to retrieval quality, so the choice should be made purely on storage cost and the engineer's personal preference
Maximum overlap is always correct because it guarantees that every answer will be found inside at least one chunk regardless of boundaries

stem: A retrieval workflow has a latency budget of 500 ms. Vector search over 50 million chunks takes 400 ms, leaving no room for reranking. Which design addresses this without discarding reranking?

choices.text: Rerank before the vector search so the expensive step happens on a smaller input set
Narrow the search space with metadata filters first so the vector search covers far fewer candidates, leaving time to rerank
Increase the latency budget to two seconds so that the full search and reranking both fit comfortably
Remove reranking entirely and accept whatever order the vector search returns, since there is no time left in the latency budget for it

stem: Answers from a RAG assistant are usually right but occasionally contain a fact from a different, unrelated document that was retrieved with a low score. What change reduces this?

choices.text: Remove the retrieval stage entirely and rely on the model's training knowledge, so that unrelated documents can never be retrieved and leak
Lower the model's temperature to zero so that it only uses the first chunk in the context
Add a relevance threshold, label injected chunks with source and score, instruct the model to cite, and verify with groundedness evaluation
Retrieve twice as many chunks so that the relevant ones outnumber the unrelated ones in the context

stem: A multilingual company has manuals in English, German and Japanese. Users ask questions in any of the three languages and expect answers from any manual. How should the retrieval index be designed?

choices.text: Translate every manual into English with a model and index only the English versions so a single-language setup can be used
Three separate indexes, one per language, with users required to pick the language of the manual they want to search before asking
Index only the English manuals, since most users can read English and this keeps the corpus small and consistent
A multilingual embedding model so queries and chunks share one vector space across languages, with language as metadata

stem: An assistant must answer questions over both a knowledge base and the user's own recent uploads (not yet in the main index). Which context strategy fits?

choices.text: Replace the main index with the uploads for the session, since the user's own documents are what they care about most
Inject the full text of every upload into every prompt for the rest of the session, since uploads are small compared with the knowledge base
Chunk and embed the uploads into a session-scoped index on the fly, merge its results with the main index, and keep provenance
Ignore the uploads until the nightly pipeline indexes them, so that all retrieval comes from one consistent index

stem: A retrieval evaluation shows that for 20% of questions the correct chunk ranks between positions 6 and 15, just outside the top 5 that are injected. What is the most efficient improvement?

choices.text: Switch to a model with a larger context window and inject the top 50 chunks for every question
Add a reranking stage over the top 30 candidates so the correct chunk is promoted into the top 5
Re-chunk the entire corpus with smaller chunks and rebuild the index from scratch
Inject the top 15 chunks for every question so the correct one is always included regardless of its position

stem: An assistant must answer questions about tabular reference data (a 5,000-row parts price list) alongside free-text manuals. How should the price list be handled for retrieval?

choices.text: Keep the price list as structured objects with exact lookup by part number, use semantic search only for manuals, and route by question type
Convert each row into a natural sentence, embed all 5,000 sentences and rely on semantic search alone to find the right price for any part
Embed the whole price list as one chunk so the model receives the full table whenever any part is mentioned
Exclude the price list from the assistant since tables cannot be used in retrieval systems

stem: An assistant retrieves from a corpus that is updated continuously. Users sometimes get an answer and, minutes later, a different answer to the same question because a new document arrived. Stakeholders ask for "stable answers". What is the appropriate response?

choices.text: Delay all new documents by a month so that answers change less often during normal use
Freeze the corpus and stop indexing new documents so that answers never change for any question
Cache every answer permanently so that the first answer given to a question is always returned afterwards, even after the corpus changes
Explain that answers reflect the current corpus; add version and timestamp to citations, and offer an "as of" mode for reproducibility

stem: A pipeline must detect which of 20 compliance topics each internal memo touches; a memo can cover several topics at once. How should the LLM step's output be designed?

choices.text: A free-text paragraph describing the topics in the memo, which analysts read when they need the classification
A single enumerated field holding the one most important topic per memo, since a memo should be filed under exactly one heading
A typed list output restricted to the 20 topic values, allowing zero or more per memo, with validation that every value is in the list
A score from 1 to 10 for how compliant the memo is, since that is what compliance reviewers care about

stem: A pipeline uses an LLM to anonymize free-text notes before they are shared with a wider audience. What verification should accompany this step?

choices.text: Deterministic post-checks (identifier patterns, name lists), sampled human review, restricted retention of originals, and a block on rows that fail
A second LLM asked whether the first one did a good job, with its answer trusted
Publishing the output and relying on readers to report any personal information they notice
None beyond the prompt, since the model was instructed to remove all personal information and modern models follow such instructions reliably

stem: Which processing placement correctly serves this requirement: "a Workshop list must sort 500,000 cases by an AI-generated urgency score"?

choices.text: In an agent that the user asks to sort the cases for them
South of the Ontology: compute the score in the pipeline and store it as a property, since sorting needs a value on every object
North of the Ontology: compute the score with a function each time the list is sorted, so that the urgency the user sees is always freshly computed
In the Workshop module itself, using a client-side script that calls the model for the visible rows

stem: An LLM transform in a Code Repository runs nightly and occasionally fails entirely when the model provider has a brief outage, leaving the dataset unbuilt for a day. What change improves resilience?

choices.text: Catch all errors and write nulls for every row so the build always succeeds
Remove the transform from the nightly schedule and run it by hand on days when the provider's status page shows that the service is stable
Switch providers every night to whichever one is up at the time
Add per-row error handling with retries, write processed rows plus a status column for failures, and reprocess only failed rows in a follow-up run

stem: A team wants an LLM to extract line items (description, quantity, unit price) from 200,000 purchase orders, which have widely varying layouts. Which prompt and output design is most robust?

choices.text: Extracting only the order total, since line items are too hard
A structured list schema, few-shot examples across layouts, arithmetic validation (quantity × price vs total), and review routing for failures
One prompt per known layout, with a manual step to classify each order's layout first
A prompt asking for a plain-text list of what the model finds, since the layouts vary far too much for any fixed structure to capture them

stem: An AI enrichment pipeline's audit requirements say that any output must be reproducible "to the extent possible". The team notes that LLM outputs are non-deterministic. What should the pipeline record and state?

choices.text: Only the final output, since that is what auditors look at
Nothing, since reproducibility is impossible with non-deterministic models and the requirement therefore cannot be met in any meaningful way
The input, prompt version, model and parameters, and the raw response, with a documented note that re-runs may differ and the stored response is the record
A hash of the output so auditors can verify it has not changed

stem: A service desk wants each new ticket enriched with a suggested resolution drawn from past tickets, visible to agents when they open it, and refreshed if the knowledge base changes. Where should the retrieval-and-suggest step run?

choices.text: Nowhere; agents should search manually
In a nightly batch only, so suggestions appear the day after a ticket is created
Entirely north: generate a fresh suggestion from retrieval every time an agent opens the ticket, so it always reflects the latest knowledge base
Index south in the pipeline; compute and store an initial suggestion on ticket creation; allow an on-demand refresh north when the agent asks

stem: An LLM classification transform's accuracy on the evaluation set is 95%, but production outputs show a category assigned to 40% of rows that the evaluation set rated at 5%. What is the likely issue?

choices.text: Production inputs differ from the suite or the prompt misfires on real inputs; sample the over-assigned rows, compare input traits, update suite and prompt
Nothing; 40% is the true rate
The model has become biased and should be retrained
The evaluation set was clearly too easy and should be deleted so that the team is no longer misled by its 95% accuracy figure

stem: A team is defining metrics for a retrieval-grounded assistant. Which set gives a complete picture of quality for release decisions?

choices.text: Correctness, groundedness, retrieval hit rate, refusal behaviour, latency and cost, each reported separately
Answer correctness alone, measured against reference answers written by the team, since a correct answer is the only thing that matters to users
User satisfaction from a survey sent after the release, since real users are the only valid judges of an assistant's quality
The number of evaluation cases that run without errors, since a case that throws an error cannot be scored and signals a broken assistant

stem: An evaluation suite for a document-processing function is built entirely from clean, well-formatted sample documents. Which additions make it representative?

choices.text: Synthetic documents generated by the same model that performs the extraction, since the model knows what inputs it handles well
Documents from a different domain entirely, since testing on unrelated material proves that the function generalizes beyond its training
Messy real cases: scanned pages, missing fields, unusual layouts, other languages, size extremes, and known-tricky production examples
More clean documents of the same kind, since a larger suite always produces a more reliable accuracy estimate for the function

stem: Two engineers get different evaluation scores for the same function version on the same day: 90% and 84%. What should be checked before concluding anything?

choices.text: Nothing; the difference is small enough to ignore, and the team should proceed with the higher of the two scores
Whether suite version, grader, model configuration or parameters differ between them, and how much the suite varies run to run
Which engineer is more experienced, since the more experienced engineer's measurement should be treated as the correct one
Whether the function was changed between the two runs, since nothing else could explain different scores on the same version

stem: An evaluation suite has grown to 2,000 cases and takes four hours to run, so engineers stop running it before small changes. What is a sound approach?

choices.text: Run the full suite only once a quarter, since four hours is too long to run more often than that for a team of this size
Stop maintaining the suite and rely on production feedback, which is faster and reflects what users actually ask
Delete most of the cases so the suite is small again, keeping only the hundred that the team finds most interesting
Tier the suite: a fast representative subset for every change, the full suite nightly and before releases

stem: Which approach to adversarial evaluation cases keeps them useful over time?

choices.text: Write a fixed set once at launch and never change it, so results remain comparable across every future version of the workflow
Maintain a living set: add new attack patterns from production and research, record the expected safe behaviour, re-run on every change
Rely on the model provider's safety testing, since they test their models against attacks more thoroughly than any application team could
Remove adversarial cases once the workflow passes them, so the suite stays focused on the cases that still fail

stem: A team wants to know whether a change improved the function for the cases that matter most to the business, not just on average. How should results be analyzed?

choices.text: Segment results by category and consequence, compare per segment before and after, and weight the decision by the segments that matter
Report only the worst case, since a single failure is enough to block any release regardless of the other results
Report the best-performing segment, since highlighting the strongest result shows stakeholders the value of the change most clearly
Report the overall average score only, since an average is the standard way to summarize any evaluation and is easy for stakeholders to read

stem: A team wants to use a model-graded evaluator to score the quality of free-text summaries produced by a function. Which statement about model-graded evaluators is accurate?

choices.text: They should never be used, because any model-based judgement is circular and cannot be trusted for evaluation purposes
They are always as reliable as human raters, so calibration against humans is unnecessary once the rubric has been written clearly
They can replace deterministic checks for numeric and categorical outputs, since a model can compare values just as well as code
They scale free-text evaluation but need explicit criteria, calibration against human ratings, and handling of their own non-determinism

stem: An AI workflow's outputs are later corrected by downstream systems (for example, finance adjusts amounts the workflow extracted). How can these corrections improve the workflow systematically?

choices.text: Ask finance to stop correcting values so the workflow's outputs remain consistent with what it originally produced
Replace the workflow with the downstream system's manual process, since the corrections show that humans do the job better anyway
Join corrections to outputs by key, measure correction rates by field and input type, turn recurring patterns into evaluation cases, prioritize fixes
They cannot, since downstream systems are separate and the workflow has no way to learn from what happens after it runs

stem: An automation should send an AI-drafted reminder to customers whose invoices become overdue, but only once per invoice and never to customers flagged as "do not contact". Which configuration expresses this?

choices.text: A manual list that an accounts clerk reviews each morning before copying the AI draft into an email for each customer by hand
A trigger on the overdue status with no further conditions, relying on the AI draft to mention that the customer should ignore the message if they have opted out of contact
A trigger on the overdue transition with conditions (not do-not-contact, no reminder sent yet) and an effect that records the reminder after sending
A daily schedule that drafts reminders for every overdue invoice and sends them all, since customers who do not want contact can reply to say so

stem: A workflow chains three functions: extract → score → decide. The decide step sometimes receives a null score because the score step silently returned nothing on model errors. What should be changed?

choices.text: Remove the score step and let the decide step work from the raw extraction alone, which avoids the null problem entirely
Make the decide step treat a null score as zero, so the workflow never stalls and every item receives a decision one way or the other
Add a fourth function that guesses a score whenever the previous step returned a null value, so downstream always has a number to work with
Make the score step return a typed error state on model errors, and route errored items to retry or review instead of passing nulls on

stem: A team must run a one-time backfill of an AI enrichment over 2 million historical objects through the same Action used by the live automation. What precautions apply?

choices.text: Run it as a bounded, rate-limited, resumable batch off-peak with idempotent writes and monitoring so live operation is not disrupted
Disable all Action validation for the backfill to avoid rejections, since historical data is known to be reliable and does not need checking
Run it as 2 million separate automation triggers, one per object, so that each object is processed exactly like a live one
Run it at full speed during business hours so it finishes quickly and the live automation can resume afterwards without any lag

stem: Which situation is best served by a function-backed Action rather than a plain Action with static rules?

choices.text: Changing a status field from Open to Closed with no computation involved, where a simple rule can validate the transition and no function is needed
Applying a change whose values are computed at execution time, such as generating a summary with an AI function and writing it with validation
Any Action at all, since function-backed Actions are strictly more capable and should be the default for every edit in the Ontology
Deleting an object, since deletion is irreversible and therefore always requires custom function logic before it can be allowed

stem: An automation's AI step was updated to a new function version last night. This morning, half of the objects processed overnight have the old output shape and half have the new one, and a downstream dashboard broke. What should have been done, and what now?

choices.text: Nothing could have prevented this, since version changes always cause temporary inconsistency and the dashboard team should have expected it
Roll back to the old version permanently so the dashboard works again and never upgrade the function in the future
Delete the objects processed overnight and let the automation reprocess them, which will restore consistency on its own
Coordinate with consumers and cut over cleanly with a compatible shape or transition; now find affected objects by version, map them to one shape, fix the dashboard

stem: A Workshop user clicks "Analyze" and the AI analysis takes 40 seconds. The team wants the button to return immediately and the result to appear when ready. Which integration supports this?

choices.text: The analysis is run in the user's browser using a lightweight model so it finishes in under a second
A synchronous function call from the button that blocks the interface until the analysis finishes, since Workshop buttons must wait for results
The button triggers an Action that records a request; an automation runs the analysis and writes the result to the object; the module shows status
The button opens a dialog asking the user to wait and refreshes the page every five seconds until the analysis completes

stem: An automation must process objects in a strict order (older first) because each decision depends on the previous one. Per-object parallel execution is producing out-of-order decisions. What should change?

choices.text: Increase the parallelism so that all objects are processed at once and the ordering problem is no longer visible to anyone
Switch to batch execution that processes objects sequentially in order within one run, or chain per-object runs so each waits for the previous
Keep parallel execution and accept occasional out-of-order decisions, since the automation will eventually process every object and small ordering errors even out
Randomize the processing order so that no particular object is consistently disadvantaged by being processed later than another

stem: Before enabling a complex multi-step AI automation in production, the team wants a rehearsal that proves the full chain works end to end without real effects. What is the best approach?

choices.text: Run it on a branch or test objects with effects pointed at non-production targets, inspect every step's output and object state, then enable with limited scope
Review the configuration on screen with the whole team and enable it if nobody can think of a problem with any of the steps
Enable it in production for one hour and watch the first effects closely, reverting any that look wrong before anyone outside the team notices
Run only the AI step on sample inputs, since the rest of the chain is just plumbing that cannot fail in interesting ways

stem: A workflow needs to process documents in Japanese, Korean and English with equal quality. The reference sheet lists one model with strong multilingual capability at medium cost and another with top English quality but weak support for Asian languages at lower cost. Which should be chosen and how verified?

choices.text: Both models, with the English one used for all documents and the multilingual one used only when the English model's output looks wrong to a reviewer
The cheaper English-focused model, since English is the most common language in the corpus and the cost saving is significant over a year
Whichever model the provider recommends for document processing, since providers understand their own models' strengths better than any customer
The multilingual model, verified with a language-stratified evaluation suite so quality per language is measured against the requirement

stem: An engineer wants to compare how two versions of a workflow behave on the same production request. Which observability capability makes this straightforward?

choices.text: Session and distributed traces recording each stage's inputs, outputs, tool calls and timing, so the two runs compare step by step
A user survey asking which version produced the more helpful answer for the request in question
The monthly cost report, which shows which version consumed more tokens and is therefore the more thorough one
Reading both versions' prompts side by side, since the prompt is the main difference between the two versions and fully determines the behaviour

stem: An agent's average latency is acceptable, but p99 latency is 30 seconds and those slow requests cluster around questions that trigger four or more tool calls. What is the best improvement?

choices.text: Switch to a faster model for all requests, since the model is the only part of the pipeline the team controls directly
Analyze slow traces: parallelize independent tool calls, cut redundant calls, cache lookups, and set a per-turn budget
Remove the slowest tool from the agent entirely, since any tool that contributes to p99 latency is not worth keeping
Cap tool calls at one per conversation turn so that no request can take more than a single call's time regardless of complexity

stem: A team wants to evaluate a new third-party model that is not yet in the platform's catalog before deciding whether to request its enablement. What is the appropriate path?

choices.text: Ask the vendor for benchmark numbers and decide based on those, since vendor benchmarks are standardized and comparable across providers
Call the model's public API directly from a Workshop widget using a developer's personal key so users can try it on real data right away
Request governed enablement in a test scope, run the suite on non-sensitive data, and decide with the results and a policy review
Use the model only through an external notebook outside the platform, copying production data into it for a realistic test

stem: Cost alerts show an AI workflow spending far more at 02:00-03:00 than at any other time, though user traffic is lowest then. What should the engineer look for?

choices.text: Automated runs in that window: a nightly automation, backfill or retry loop, visible in execution history and telemetry by caller
A pricing change by the provider that applies only at night, which would explain why the same traffic costs more during those hours
Users in other time zones, since 02:00 locally is daytime elsewhere and their requests are naturally longer and more expensive
Nothing unusual, since AI costs fluctuate randomly and a nightly spike is within normal variation for any workflow

stem: A workflow must run in a jurisdiction that requires data to stay in-region. The reference sheet shows the best-performing model hosted out of region, and an in-region model with slightly lower scores. Which choice is correct?

choices.text: The out-of-region model, since quality is the primary selection criterion and the residency rule can be satisfied by encrypting the data in transit
The in-region model, since geography is a hard constraint; verify it meets the quality threshold on the suite and document the decision
The out-of-region model with a prompt instruction telling it not to store the data, which satisfies the regulation's intent
Neither; the workflow should be cancelled because no single model is both the best performing and hosted in the required region

stem: An AI workflow's token usage per request has crept up 60% over three months without any deliberate change. Which observability practice would have caught this earlier, and what is the fix?

choices.text: Reviewing the monthly invoice line by line, which would have shown the gradual increase early and prompted the team to shorten the system prompt
Switching to a cheaper model each quarter so that gradual growth in tokens is offset by a lower price per token
Capping the model's maximum output tokens, which limits the cost of every request regardless of what caused the growth
Trending tokens per request with a drift alert, then diagnosing with traces which component grew and bounding it

stem: A production workflow uses a provider model that the provider announces will be deprecated in 60 days. What should the AI engineer do?

choices.text: Wait until the deprecation date and switch to whatever replacement the provider offers at that time, since there is no way to prepare in advance
Pin the deprecated model indefinitely by contract with the provider so that nothing in the workflow has to change
Select a replacement now, run the evaluation suite, adjust prompts, roll it out as a versioned change with rollback, and make the model change visible
Switch immediately to a different provider's model without evaluation, since any model is better than one that is about to be deprecated

stem: An agent is available to the whole company, but one of its tools queries a dataset that only the finance group may read. How should the configuration handle this so that permissions are respected without breaking the agent for everyone else?

choices.text: Remove the tool from the agent entirely, since any tool with restricted data cannot be offered in a company-wide agent
Run the tool under each user's own permissions, so finance users get results and others get an empty result the agent explains
Run the tool under a privileged service identity so that all users receive finance results regardless of their own permissions
Give every user the finance marking so the tool works for all of them, since an agent that fails for most users is a poor experience

stem: A customer asks a company to delete their personal data. The company's AI workflows have stored chunk embeddings, raw model responses and generated summaries containing that customer's data. What must the AI engineer's design support?

choices.text: Traceability from the customer to every derived artefact (chunks, vectors, raw responses, outputs) so deletion can be executed and verified
Deletion only of artefacts that are visible to users, since internal artefacts cannot cause harm to the customer
Deletion of the source record only, since downstream artefacts will be rebuilt automatically from scratch by the next pipeline run
Nothing, since derived artefacts such as embeddings and summaries are not personal data and are exempt from deletion requests

stem: An AI function flags transactions as potential fraud for an investigations team. Which design respects the consequence of a wrong flag for the customer?

choices.text: Notify the customer directly by email that they are suspected of fraud, so they can defend themselves before any internal investigation starts
Automatically freeze the customer's account on any flag, since speed matters more than accuracy when fraud is suspected
Ignore flags below a confidence of 99% so that only near-certain cases are ever reviewed by the investigations team
Treat the flag as a recommendation with reasons; an investigator decides any customer-impacting action; monitor false positives; allow appeals

stem: Security review finds that an agent's tool can accept an arbitrary query string that the model composes. A crafted conversation made the model compose a query that returned records outside the intended scope. What is the right fix?

choices.text: Add a prompt instruction telling the model to compose only safe queries that stay strictly within the current user's own records and nothing else
Log all queries the model composes and review them weekly for scope violations
Constrain the tool: replace free-form query strings with typed parameters bound to the user's scope, and run it under the user's permissions
Limit the tool to returning at most ten records, which bounds how much data a crafted query can expose

stem: A department wants to turn off the organization's capacity limits for AI usage because their workflow was throttled during a busy week. What should the AI engineer recommend?

choices.text: Turn off the limits for everyone, since throttling legitimate work is worse than any risk from unlimited usage
Turn off the limits for that department only, since they have demonstrated a real need and will manage their own usage
Keep the limits; analyze and optimize the throttled workflow, then request a justified, monitored capacity increase for it
Advise the department to split their workflow across several accounts to stay under each account's limit

stem: A company must be able to answer, for any AI-generated recommendation, "which version of which policy document did the model rely on". What does the retrieval design need?

choices.text: A copy of the entire policy library attached to every recommendation so that any version can be found later if needed
Chunks carrying document id and version metadata, injected with those ids, and outputs recording the cited chunk ids
A note in the system prompt listing the policy documents the model is allowed to use for its recommendations
The model's own statement of which policy it used, included in its answer text for auditors to read

stem: Which design correctly applies "match validation strictness to consequence" for an AI workflow that both answers product questions and can issue store credit?

choices.text: Strict validation for product answers because they are frequent and errors add up, and light validation for store credit because it is rare
No validation for either, since the workflow is customer-facing and validation would slow down responses for customers
Apply the same strict human approval to every output, including product answers, so that the workflow is uniformly safe
Light validation (groundedness, refusal path) for product answers; strict validation, limits and approval for store credit, with audit

stem: A company deploys an AI agent that reads incoming documents from external parties. Which combination best reflects defence in depth against prompt injection for this agent?

choices.text: Content isolation, least-privilege tools, no consequential Actions on document content alone, input/output checks, approval, monitoring, tests
Blocking all external documents from being processed by the agent, which removes the possibility of injection altogether at the cost of the use case
A single strong system prompt instruction to ignore any instructions found within documents, reviewed quarterly by the security team
Relying on the model provider's built-in safety features, since modern models are trained to recognize and ignore injected instructions

stem: A Logic function must return a decision of "approve", "reject" or "escalate" together with a short reason and a confidence between 0 and 1. The consuming automation branches on the decision. How should the output be declared?

choices.text: A free-text paragraph in which the model explains its decision in detail for a human to read before the automation acts
A struct output with an enumerated decision, a string reason and a numeric confidence, so the automation branches on a typed field
Three separate outputs on three different functions that the automation calls one after another and then combines
A single string output such as "approve: looks fine (0.8)" that the automation parses with a regular expression on every run it processes

stem: An engineer must decide whether a text-normalization step (trimming whitespace, standardizing date formats, mapping country codes) should be a Logic completion or deterministic code inside the function. What is the right call?

choices.text: A Logic completion, because language models are good at text and will handle unusual cases that code would miss
A tool-using reasoning block that looks up each country code in a reference table before the model normalizes the rest of the text itself
A Logic completion with temperature set to zero, which makes the model as reliable as code for formatting tasks
Deterministic code (a code function or expression block), since the rules are explicit and must give identical results every run

stem: A Logic function started returning answers in a different language for some inputs after a model version change by the provider. The prompt was unchanged. How should the engineer respond?

choices.text: Add a post-processing translation step that translates every answer to the expected language regardless of what the model returned
Switch the function to a completely different provider immediately, since any provider that changes models cannot be relied on
Confirm the version change in traces, add a language instruction and output validation, extend the suite, manage the version
Assume the provider will fix it and wait, since the prompt did not change and nothing on the function's side needs adjustment

stem: A function must call a legacy calculation that exists only as a published TypeScript function in the Ontology. The result feeds the prompt. How is this integrated in AIP Logic?

choices.text: Add the published function as a tool in the Logic function and inject its typed result into the prompt as a variable
Ask the model to guess the calculation's result from similar past outputs that are included as examples in the prompt
Re-implement the calculation inside the prompt by describing the formula in words and asking the model to compute it
Export the legacy function's results to a spreadsheet each night and paste the relevant row into the function's input

stem: A Logic function's evaluation suite passes, but an engineer wants to understand the single worst-scoring case before publishing. Which trace elements are most informative?

choices.text: The function's overall latency, since slow runs tend to be the wrong ones
The temperature setting, since variance explains most low-scoring cases
The resolved prompt, each tool call with its result, the raw model response and the parsed output, read in order to find the failing stage
Only the final output, since the score is computed from it alone and nothing else in the run matters for understanding the failure

stem: A Logic function applies an edit that sets `owner` on a Case object. In production, some cases were assigned to users who had left the company. What safeguard belongs in the function?

choices.text: A lookup that checks the proposed owner against active users before the edit, routing invalid ones to review
A prompt instruction asking the model to choose only owners who are current employees, with a list of departed employees to avoid
A larger model that is less likely to suggest former employees
A weekly report listing cases assigned to inactive users for manual correction

stem: Which block arrangement in AIP Logic best handles "if the input document is longer than 20 pages, summarize it first; otherwise answer the question directly"?

choices.text: A single completion that receives the whole document and is told to summarize it first if it seems long
A conditional on a measured page or token count that routes long documents through a summarization completion before answering
Two separate functions, one for long and one for short documents, with every caller expected to measure the length and pick the right one
A loop that summarizes every document regardless of length to keep the flow simple

stem: Two engineers disagree about a Logic function's prompt: one wants a long prompt with twenty rules and examples; the other wants a short prompt. The function's suite scores 92% with the long prompt and 91% with the short one, at half the tokens. The function runs 50,000 times a day. Which should be published?

choices.text: Alternate daily between the two to average the cost and the score
The long prompt, because a higher evaluation score always wins regardless of the token cost or the daily volume of calls
Neither, until a prompt reaches 100% on the suite
The short prompt, since one point is within variance and the saving is substantial; confirm with repeated runs first

stem: A plant-maintenance team wants an agent that works on shop-floor tablets inside their existing Workshop module, reacting to the machine the technician taps. Which deployment and configuration fit?

choices.text: A standalone agent page that technicians open separately and into which they type the machine number from the tablet screen
AIP Assist configured with the plant's manuals, since it is already present on every page of the platform
The agent embedded in the Workshop module with the tapped machine passed as application state and tools scoped to that machine
A scheduled function that generates a daily troubleshooting sheet per machine for technicians to read in the morning

stem: An agent gives inconsistent answers to the same question depending on the order in which retrieved documents appear in its context. What configuration helps most?

choices.text: Randomize the document order on every run so that no single order dominates the answers over time and the bias averages out
Rank context deterministically by relevance, deduplicate overlaps, label sources, and instruct the agent to synthesize across them
Reduce retrieval to one document so order no longer matters
Increase the temperature so that the agent explores all of the retrieved documents equally instead of focusing on the first one

stem: Before releasing an agent that answers tax-related questions for employees, which review beyond engineering evaluation is appropriate?

choices.text: A vote among the engineering team on whether the sampled answers look reasonable to them before the agent is switched on
None; evaluation scores above the agreed threshold are sufficient evidence for release in any subject area, tax included
A review by the model provider, who certifies the agent for tax content
A domain review by qualified tax or legal staff of sample answers and refusal boundaries, with findings turned into cases

stem: An agent should answer in the user's language, but its instructions and documents are in English. Which configuration makes this work reliably?

choices.text: Instructing the agent to respond in the user's language, using multilingual retrieval or query translation, and testing per language
Asking users to write their questions in English, since the documents and instructions are in English and mixing languages is risky
Translating all of the documents into every supported language with a model before indexing, so that each language has its own corpus
Detecting the language and routing to a separate agent per language

stem: Which situation calls for a standalone agent rather than an embedded one?

choices.text: An agent whose Actions always operate on the record that is currently displayed in the application the user has open
A workflow in which every question concerns the particular object that the user has selected on screen in an application
A company-wide assistant for general process questions that users open from anywhere, with no application context
A troubleshooting assistant that needs the module's current filter state and visible rows in order to answer correctly

stem: An agent in production is frequently asked questions outside its intended scope (HR questions to a logistics agent). What should be configured?

choices.text: Scope instructions that recognize out-of-scope requests and redirect, with evaluation cases and monitoring of their frequency
Let the agent answer anyway from the model's general knowledge, since a plausible answer is better than a redirect
Block users who repeatedly ask out-of-scope questions so that the agent's logs and metrics only reflect its intended use
Expand the agent's scope, retrieval context and tools to cover every topic that users have asked about so far

stem: An agent has a tool that can create objects and another that can only read. The team debates whether to require user confirmation before the create tool runs. What is the right design?

choices.text: Confirmation only when the user seems unsure about what they want, as judged by the model from the tone of the conversation
Confirmation or a review Action for the create tool, none for read tools, with the confirmation showing what will be created
Confirmation for every single tool call, including read-only lookups, so that the experience is consistent across all tools
No confirmation for either tool, since confirmations slow users down and the agent is usually right about what they wanted

stem: A company plans to retire an agent and replace it with a new design. Users have active conversations and saved links. What release practice applies?

choices.text: Keep the old agent running forever alongside the new one so that no user is ever disrupted by the change
Delete the old agent immediately when the new one is published, so that nobody keeps using the design that is being retired
Rename the old agent to the new name and swap its instructions, tools and context in place so that existing links keep working
Run both for a transition, redirect links, close conversations gracefully, communicate, and remove the old agent once usage drops

stem: A retrieval corpus contains both long narrative reports and short FAQ entries. Users complain that FAQ answers are drowned out by report chunks. Which indexing design helps?

choices.text: Indexing both with a document-type metadata field, preferring FAQ entries for question-shaped queries, and keeping chunk sizes comparable
Merging each FAQ entry into the nearest report so that the corpus has a single uniform document type
Removing the reports from the index so that only the FAQ entries can ever be retrieved for any question
Increasing the number of retrieved chunks so that the FAQ entries are statistically more likely to appear somewhere in the context

stem: A legal assistant must never cite a document the user is not entitled to see, even in a passing reference. Where in the retrieval pipeline must the permission filter run, and why not later?

choices.text: At display time, hiding links the user cannot open while leaving the answer text intact
Before ranking, by executing the search as the user so unauthorized chunks are never candidates and cannot influence the answer
After generation, scanning the finished answer for the titles of documents the user cannot see and removing any sentences that mention them
Nowhere, since legal documents are internal and all employees are trusted

stem: Retrieval quality dropped after the corpus grew from 100,000 to 5 million chunks, although the embedding model and chunking are unchanged. What is the most likely cause and remedy?

choices.text: The embedding model cannot handle large corpora and must be replaced with a bigger one
The index is corrupted and must be rebuilt from an empty state before it works again
Many more near-neighbours crowd the top results; add metadata filters, reranking over a larger candidate set, and deduplication
Users are simply asking harder questions now that the corpus is bigger, and nothing in the retrieval system itself has changed

stem: A workflow must answer questions that require combining facts from several documents (for example, comparing two suppliers' contract terms). Which retrieval approach supports this?

choices.text: Retrieving the entire contracts of both suppliers into the context regardless of length
A single top-1 retrieval for the whole question, since the single best chunk will contain the comparison if one exists anywhere
Asking the user to compare the suppliers themselves after the assistant returns one representative chunk per supplier for them to read
Multi-query retrieval: decompose into sub-questions per supplier and aspect, retrieve for each, deduplicate, and inject labelled evidence
